g.text: How 993 bytes recognize a handwritten digit
One image, four phases. The pictures and scores below come from the frozen model.
Turn pixels into eight response maps
Each filter scans 3 × 3 patches and responds to a different learned pattern.
These are eight responses to one image.
Each square keeps the image’s layout.
Darker areas show where a filter
Update twice, shrink, then do it again
The four updates reuse one set of weights. Shrinking reduces the number of positions to process.
Mix information from all eight maps, add it to the existing maps,
and replace negative values with zero. Do this twice.
Keep the largest number in each 2 × 2 patch.
That halves the width and height of every map.
One of the eight maps is shown at each stage above; all eight are updated together.
Turn the maps into 48 numbers, then ten digit scores
Six regional averages per map preserve a rough sense of where the responses are.
Their average becomes the outlined summary cell.
For each digit: multiply the 48 values by that digit’s
48 learned weights, add the results, then add its bias.
Try 25 shifted views, average by digit, and choose
Run phases 1–3 on 25 shifted views. For each digit, add its 25 scores and divide by 25.
Numbers are rounded for display. Activation colors are scaled separately at each stage.
